$comment: MULTI-CU runtime witness for stdio.json's pe `sprintf` COMPILER-SYNTHESIZED shim (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION, Phase 3) -- the cross-CU sibling of the single-source `shipped_sprintf_ucrt`. WHY BOTH EXIST: the two drivers place the shim synthesis at DIFFERENT points in the pipeline and are NOT equivalent. The single-CU driver (compile_pipeline.cpp) synthesizes the shim POST-optimize inside `lowerCuMirToAssembly`, so the optimizer never sees the shim body; the multi-CU driver (program.cpp) reconstructs the recipe map from the MERGED symbol names and synthesizes PRE-optimize, so `optimizeModule`'s full release pipeline -- Inlining, ConstFold, Mem2Reg, CopyProp, Cse, Licm, SimplifyCfg, Dce -- then runs OVER the synthesized body. The REAL consumer, the sqlite testfixture, is a multi-CU `--project` build, so the pe64 sprintf fix actually ships through the second seam, which had NO runtime witness at all before this example. ★ THE SPECIFIC SILENT MISCOMPILE ONLY THIS EXAMPLE CAN CATCH: after the merge the inliner RESOLVES `sprintf` to the synthesized definition (an intra-module function, no longer an extern), and the shim body is a single block of ~10 instructions -- far under release.pipeline.json's `inlineThreshold` of 50. The ONLY thing preventing it from being spliced into its caller is the callee refusal in src/opt/passes/inlining.cpp for any body containing a `VaHomeArgAreaAddr` / `VaRegSaveAreaAddr` / `VaOverflowArgAreaAddr` leaf: those lower to `lea reg, [sp+off]` against the CALLEE's OWN frame (only the callee's variadic prologue spills the home area), so a spliced shim would derive `ap` from the CALLER's frame -- which spilled nothing -- and read garbage. It compiles, links, runs, and prints WRONG TEXT. Nothing pinned that refusal at runtime before this example, and no single-source example can reach it, because under the single-CU seam the shim does not exist until the optimizer has already finished. RED-ON-DISABLE (release arm): delete the VaHomeArgAreaAddr line from the inlining.cpp refusal and the release arm's formatted output goes wrong (baseline, which runs no Inlining, stays green -- which is exactly why the `release` arm is the point of this example). SHAPE: fmt.c owns every operand as a MUTABLE global plus four tiny `return sprintf(...)` wrappers that are themselves inline candidates, so Inlining first splices each wrapper into main and thereby places the sprintf call site in main's body, where the shim-inline refusal is then actually consulted; main.c ALSO calls sprintf directly on fmt.c's globals, so BOTH TUs carry a call site and both must bind the SAME merged shim. COVERAGE: an int vararg, a lone `double` (the Win64 xmm->home-slot spill no integer check can reach), int+double INTERLEAVED in both orders (the positional-ordering case a contiguous-spill bug still passes the lone-double check on), a 64-bit `long long` past INT32_MAX, unsigned hex, and the real sqlite shellDtostr() shape `%#+.*e` (a star-precision int vararg consumed BEFORE a double, whose two-digit exponent also fails loudly if the pe binding ever regresses from ucrtbase to legacy msvcrt's three-digit form). Finally main WRITES `g_pos` and re-reads it through fmt.c's wrapper, which pins the merge as ONE storage (two per-CU copies would still print 12345) and proves the formatting happens at RUNTIME rather than being const-folded. ANTI-FOLD: every operand is a mutable global, never a literal. All values are exactly representable with no rounding tie, so the expected text is identical under UCRT, glibc and Darwin libc; the strings were derived INDEPENDENTLY by compiling the same two sources with real gcc 13.3.0 and running them (exit 42 at both -O0 and -O2), not by hand. elf/macho keep importing the real libc `sprintf` unchanged (stdio.json's split is [elf,macho] plain-FFI vs [pe] synthesize), so the same sources on all four hosted targets are also a cross-target agreement check. exit = 42; a distinct code per check (50..63).
